Arc Institute is hiring a Software Engineer for its Infrastructure Engineering team to support and operate the laboratory information management system (LIMS). The role maintains lab data systems, supports scientists and their tools, improves data quality, and automates recurring requests.
Biotechnology
Non Profit
Education
Training
H1B Sponsor Likely
Responsibilities
Run the request queue for Arc's lab data systems, from questions and fixes to schema changes, which you'll ship through our change workflow so other teams' pipelines don't break
Support the templates scientists record experiments with, and the command-line tools that pull their data for analysis
Run training sessions for scientists, and write the docs they come back to
Build and maintain the checks that catch errors in data as scientists enter it, so bad records don't reach analysis or pipelines
Help carry out the refactor of the team and permission structure in our LIMS, which decides who can see and edit what
Turn the requests that keep coming back into automation, and choose the approach that fits the problem: a script, a scheduled job, a template change or an AI agent. Write the runbook, add the checks and retire the manual step; changes go through the team's code review
Build tools that make screen and experiment metadata queryable across systems for computational biologists and lab teams
Run the request queue and ship schema changes on your own, with the Tech Lead reviewing designs instead of each change
Own a part of the lab platform from design through support
Qualification
Python
SQL
REST APIs
Debugging
AI Coding Tools
Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS)
Electronic Lab Notebooks (ELN)
Lab Data
Automation Scripting
CI Pipelines
Software Testing
Required
Bachelor's degree with 0-2 years of relevant experience, or an advanced degree
You write solid Python and SQL, and you're comfortable working with REST APIs
You debug problems in systems you didn't build, working from the code, logs and data
You use AI coding tools day to day or are ready to learn, you check what they produce, and you're careful with sensitive research data
You explain technical things clearly to scientists, and you write docs and training that people use
You ask for help early and take feedback well
You've owned a piece of work from start to finish, in school, an internship or a job, and you stayed responsible for it after it shipped
Preferred
You've used a LIMS or ELN, such as Benchling, or you've worked with lab data like samples and sequencing metadata
You've automated a repeated manual task with scripts, bots or agents
You've worked on CI pipelines, tests or repo templates
You've supported the users of a tool, on a help desk, as a TA or on an on-call rotation
Benefits
Annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.
Eligibility to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”), providing multi-year cash grants with a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute.
Work onsite in the Palo Alto office at least 3 days a week.
